text:
Marathon Petroleum ticked up 0.89% today after bouncing back from yesterday's 1.5% decline. The recovery sits within a broader two-week rally of nearly 9%, driven by elevated oil prices—US crude is trading at $97.26 per barrel, well above historical norms—and refinery utilization at a robust 97.8%. Higher crude prices expand the profit margins refiners earn by processing oil into gasoline and diesel, directly boosting their bottom line.

The geopolitical backdrop remains volatile: Saudi Arabia's forced shutdown of a major crude pipeline this week after drone attacks, combined with the Iran conflict keeping crude above $100 in recent sessions, has kept energy prices elevated. While Trump's recent comments suggest oil could fall sharply post-election if tensions ease, the near-term supply constraints and high refinery demand are sustaining the conditions that favor refiner earnings.
